# Dushan Tenon updater adapter

Source: unmodified crates.io `tauri-plugin-updater 2.13.1` release snapshot,
upstream `tauri-apps/plugins-workspace`, `plugins/updater`,
commit `e51128438011755f9e7277bad29b8c0978cf281c`.
Published crate SHA-256:
`3cb0b2ea3e85ca287990d3859a29cc5cb18024240fd78f62e027fb7963670f18`.

This project selects the MIT license. `LICENSE_MIT`, `LICENSE_APACHE-2.0`,
the upstream copyright notices and SPDX declarations remain unchanged.
S11 supplied the snapshot and its manifest adaptations before this slice.
The enabled feature set remains **rustls-tls only**. The Unix adapter below
adds a direct target-specific reference to the already locked rustix 1.1.5 fs
API and removes unused Linux dirs/macOS osakit dependencies; no new version or
ZIP/system-proxy feature is introduced.

## Patches

1. **Explicit Windows scratch.** `UpdaterBuilder::scratch_root` accepts an
   absolute existing directory supplied and validated by the host.
   `make_temp_dir` uses only `tempdir_in` below that root; installer files use
   `tempfile_in` below the resulting directory. Missing, relative and
   unwritable paths fail. There is no system temporary-directory fallback.
   The host checks every component of its explicit scratch path for links and
   Windows reparse points. All platforms use
   `<state-root>/Temp/updates/<random id>/`.
2. **Bounded metadata and downloads.** `MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 1 MiB` and
   `MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES = 250 MiB`. Check Content-Length before accumulating,
   then use checked addition before extending each chunk. Chunked responses
   have the same limits. `Error::DownloadTooLarge` maps to the safe host code
   `app.update.download_too_large`; no truncation is accepted. Append validated
   chunks with `extend_from_slice`, avoiding byte-by-byte debug-build iteration
   when exercising the full 250 MiB boundary.
3. **Shutdown and installer seam.** `Update::on_before_exit` replaces the
   upstream cleanup callback with the host's blocking-worker bridge. The
   bridge waits for the existing ExitController/Started shutdown, then calls
   Tauri cleanup. `UpdaterBuilder::installer_launcher` is a narrow replacement
   for the actual launch operation in tests. An injected launcher returns
   without exiting the test process; production leaves it unset and retains
   the upstream ShellExecuteW and successful process exit path.
4. **Rust-only plugin.** Remove guest commands, `api-iife.js`, their
   autogenerated permissions/schema/default permission, invoke_handler and
   global JS registration. The build script registers an empty command list,
   as the window-state adapter does. Only the application's four
   `allow-app-update-*` permissions belong in main capability.
5. **rustls-tls-only compilation.** Gate `Cursor` by the platforms/features
   which actually use it. No system-proxy or zip feature is enabled.

6. **S14: existing HTTP types.** Re-export only `reqwest::Proxy` and
   `reqwest::redirect::Policy`. The host has no direct reqwest dependency and
   needs these types to construct authenticated proxies and disable redirects
   in configure_client. No dependency, manifest, lockfile or feature changes.

7. **Explicit Unix installation (2026-10-27).** `src/unix_install.rs` replaces
   the upstream macOS and Linux installers. Only standard `.app.tar.gz` and
   bare v2 Type 2 `.AppImage` artifacts are accepted. Linux deb/rpm, sudo,
   password prompts, AppleScript, system-temp/cache fallback, and v1 AppImage
   tar installation are removed. `scratch_root` and `on_before_exit` now work
   on all three desktop platforms. The host still controls authorization,
   proxy snapshots, signatures, download limits, and complete shutdown.
8. **Bounded Mac archives.** Before extraction, a raw tar pass limits each
   GNU long-name header to 64 KiB, each file to 512 MiB, actual decompressed
   bytes including headers/padding to 1 GiB, and all entries to 20,000.
   Only regular files, directories and GNU long-name metadata are allowed;
   all soft/hard links, devices, sparse files and PAX extensions are rejected.
   The second pass validates one exact current `.app` root, ordinary relative
   path components, 4096-byte paths, duplicate/case-colliding destinations,
   and filesystem-resolved aliases. Files are created exclusively, executable
   bits are bounded to 0777, and the expected main Mach-O and Info.plist must
   exist. Trailing nonzero tar bytes, extra gzip members and bad gzip checksums
   fail. The v2 AppImage path validates ELF64, machine and Type 2 magic, stages
   the bytes before shutdown and preserves the original executable permissions.
9. **Atomic exchange and retained evidence.** Unix scratch must be ordinary,
   canonical, beneath the explicit host-injected operation directory, and on
   the target volume. Every directory component is checked without following
   links; the path is independent of a desktop launcher's working directory. Preparation
   never changes the installed product. A synchronized journal records both
   object identities and locations before the host's shutdown hook. Identities
   are rechecked after shutdown, then rustix `renameat_with(EXCHANGE)` performs
   the single atomic exchange (Linux renameat2 / macOS renameatx_np RENAME_SWAP).
   There is no move-away gap and no non-atomic fallback. A post-exchange sync or
   journal failure exchanges the objects back and records rolled_back when
   storage permits; rollback failure is returned, with both objects retained.
   The host retains the parent candidate directory before installation and
   requests the existing Tauri restart only after success. These operations do
   not guarantee recovery from every power-loss/filesystem failure. The
   prepared/installed/rolled_back journal and old object remain available for
   explicit recovery; no automatic destructive recovery is added.

## Rust standard-library fragment provenance

The comment on `escape_nsis_current_exe_arg` in `src/updater.rs` records an
adaptation of [`rust-lang/rust`, commit
`1c047506f94cd2d05228eb992b0a6bbed1942349`,
`library/std/src/sys/args/windows.rs`, line 174](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1c047506f94cd2d05228eb992b0a6bbed1942349/library/std/src/sys/args/windows.rs#L174).
The upstream file has no per-file license header. The repository-root
`COPYRIGHT` at that commit states dual Apache-2.0/MIT licensing and attributes
copyright to The Rust Project Contributors, verified on 2026-10-20.
The adapted fragment is used under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; this project selects
MIT. The full license text is included in the repository-root
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. This provenance is separate from the plugin's Tauri
copyright. Preserve the source comment.

The vendor directory's `LICENSE.spdx` is legacy upstream package metadata
(`PackageName: tauri`), preserved unchanged; it is not this repository's SPDX
inventory.

## Migration into Dushan Tenon

The adapter test module and function names omit the historical phase prefix.
Product references in patch comments use Dushan Tenon. No production vendor
implementation or signature fixture changed in this migration.

## Tests and release boundary

The adapter tests cover missing/relative/non-directory scratch paths, declared
and actual metadata limits, download size limits, real minisign verification,
wrong keys, altered bytes, version mismatch, and injected installer ordering.
Host tests exercise ownership, opaque cancellation, delayed shutdown and
stopped-after-install-failure behavior. No test starts a real installer.
Actual command results are recorded in `Temp/p4r-p6/result-09.md`.

The plugin is excluded from the workspace. Cargo rejects testing it directly
as a non-member with dev-dependencies; that is not a passing test result.
These vendor unit tests cannot run in place; the critical behavior is covered
through host tests using MockRuntime, synthetic signatures, loopback servers
and an injected installer launcher.

Windows artifacts must be **bare NSIS `.exe` or MSI `.msi` plus a detached
minisign signature** (`bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true`).
`v1Compatible` and installer ZIP artifacts are forbidden. The payload fixture
is synthetic bytes beginning with MZ, not a runnable installer.
Authenticode signing and real installation remain P7 acceptance work.

## Regenerating public signature fixtures

Use the checked-in Tauri CLI under the task's isolated C0 environment:

```powershell
node node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js signer generate --ci -w Temp/p6-09/keys/test.key
node node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js signer sign -f Temp/p6-09/keys/test.key --app-version 0.2.0 Temp/p6-09/payload.bin
```

The payload is ASCII `MZsynthetic P6-09 signature fixture; not an installer`
followed by LF. Copy only `test.key.pub`, the payload and its `.sig` to
`tests/fixtures/{public-key.txt,payload.bin,valid.sig}`. Generate a second
one-time key under the same task directory and sign the same payload/version
to produce `wrong-key.sig`. Delete both private keys immediately after use;
never copy a private key to the repository fixtures or logs.

Release public keys and URLs are not test fixtures: `src-tauri/release.json`
remains `null`. Keep test material out of the production release configuration.

## Provenance verification

Verified on 2026-10-20 against the original crates.io
`tauri-plugin-updater-2.13.1.crate` release archive. Its SHA-256 is
`3cb0b2ea3e85ca287990d3859a29cc5cb18024240fd78f62e027fb7963670f18`,
matching both the value recorded above and the crates.io sparse-index `cksum`.

A file-by-file comparison of the unpacked archive with this directory found:

- `LICENSE_APACHE-2.0`, `LICENSE_MIT` and `LICENSE.spdx` are byte-for-byte
  identical to the originals.
- The only files with changed contents are `Cargo.toml` (`publish = false`
  and a standalone `[workspace]` with `resolver = "3"`), `build.rs` (no guest
  command or global JS registration), `src/error.rs` (`DownloadTooLarge`),
  `src/lib.rs` (remove the guest command module/handler and re-export
  `reqwest::{Proxy, redirect::Policy}`), and `src/updater.rs` (the adaptations
  described in Patches 1–9 and the added `adapter_tests` module).
- Only in this directory: `PATCHES.md`, `src/unix_install.rs` and `tests/fixtures/` containing
  `payload.bin`, `public-key.txt`, `valid.sig` and `wrong-key.sig`.
- Only in the release archive: `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
  `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml.orig`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `api-iife.js`,
  `src/commands.rs`, `permissions/default.toml`,
  `permissions/schemas/schema.json`, `permissions/autogenerated/reference.md`,
  and `permissions/autogenerated/commands/{check,download,download_and_install,install}.toml`.
  The JavaScript API script, command module and generated permissions/schema
  were removed together as described in Patch 4.

The `verify_signature` function body and its call in `Update::download` in
`src/updater.rs` are identical to the originals. Neither the function nor the
download call overlaps any hunk in the file diff with three context lines;
signature verification has not been modified.

The 2026-10-27 Unix tests exercise file and nonempty-directory atomic exchange,
shutdown ordering, a changed target, journal-failure rollback, scratch/link
rejection, raw AppImage headers and permissions, and malicious Mac archive
paths/links/duplicates/metadata budgets. They use only explicit Temp fixtures
and never execute an artifact, installer, privileged command or updater restart.
Run the vendor crate's tests from an isolated workspace with the same locked
dependencies on Linux/macOS; the historical in-place test limitation above is
not a passing result. Host release-config and lifecycle tests remain required.
